selectiveHotelling: Selective Hotelling T-squared Testing After Clustering with Unknown Covariance

Source: R/selectiveHotelling-package.R
selectiveHotelling-package.Rd

Tests whether two clusters found by a clustering algorithm have the same mean, with Hotelling's \(T^2\) and an unknown covariance matrix \(\Sigma\). The p-values condition on the clustering and on the statistics that remove the unknown means and \(\Sigma\), so they control the selective Type I error.

Main functions

  • selective_hotelling_test() - clusters the data (k-means or hierarchical clustering) and runs the main test.

  • selective_hotelling_bc() - the main test for any clustering function cl_fun: the Besag and Clifford (1989) construction with the random Givens kernel on the event that the clustering returns the tested pair. The p-value is exactly uniform under the null for any path length and any reversible kernel; the kernel and the path length affect only power.

  • selective_truncated_F() - the one-dimensional test, which also fixes all of the polar factor except one angle. It is computed by the same construction on the angle for any clustering function, and in closed form for k-means when the conditioning includes the whole Lloyd trajectory.

  • kmeans_fun() / kmeans_with_fixed_init() - k-means with its trajectory.

  • hclust_fun() - hierarchical clustering (squared-distance default).

  • hotelling_T2() - the two-sample Hotelling \(T^2\) statistic.

  • generate_exchangeable_null_data() - simulate null data.

References

Besag, J. and Clifford, P. (1989). Generalized Monte Carlo significance tests. Biometrika, 76(4), 633-642.

Chen, Y. T. and Witten, D. M. (2023). Selective inference for k-means clustering. Journal of Machine Learning Research.

Gao, L. L., Bien, J. and Witten, D. (2024). Selective inference for hierarchical clustering. Journal of the American Statistical Association.
